channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: How Aliko Dangote built a $31.9 billion fortune without tech
item.description: Aliko Dangote is now worth $31.9 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. His wealth has risen by $1.89 billion this year, including a recent daily gain of $50.8 million. His biggest earner, Dangote Oil Refinery, Africa’s largest refinery, began operating in early 2024.

item.title: Morocco's largest telecoms operator reports $760 million profit in 2025
item.description: Maroc Telecom, Morocco’s largest telecommunications operator, said its net profit rose sharply to 6.97 billion dirhams ($760 million) in 2025, boosted by comparison with a weak result a year earlier linked to a regulatory settlement.

item.title: From job promises to warfronts: Nigeria warns its youths about a deadly foreign trap
item.description: Nigeria recently issued a warning to its citizens regarding the illegal enlistment of foreigners in the Ukraine/Russia conflict.

item.title: Mali and Canadian miner reset ties over $900 million gold asset with 10-year deal
item.description: Mali’s military-led government has approved a draft decree extending the operating permit for Barrick Mining’s Loulo-Gounkoto gold complex by a further 10 years, marking a decisive end to a prolonged dispute that unsettled one of Africa’s most important gold assets.

item.title: Global trader Vitol backs $3billion gas plant in Africa’s most industrialised country
item.description: Global commodity trader Vitol is backing a consortium developing a planned $3 billion gas-fired power station and liquefied natural gas (LNG) import terminal at South Africa’s Durban port, according to a company spokesperson.

item.title: South Africa's billionaire Patrice Motsepe exits executive role in his $2.7 billion mining empire
item.description: South African billionaire Patrice Motsepe has stepped down as executive chairman of African Rainbow Minerals, marking a significant leadership shift at the mining group he founded and built into a $2.7 billion enterprise (Market Cap).

item.title: 100 U.S military advisers arrive in Nigeria under expanded security agreement
item.description: The Defence Headquarters in Nigeria (DHQ) has confirmed the arrival of about 100 United States military personnel and associated equipment at Bauchi Airfield, marking the latest phase in bilateral security cooperation aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s counterterrorism capabilities.

item.title: Italian oil giant uncovers three trillion cubic feet of gas in Ivory Coast’s second-largest offshore find
item.description: Italian energy giant Eni has announced a major natural gas and condensate discovery offshore Côte d'Ivoire, marking the second-largest hydrocarbon find in the country’s history.

item.title: Nigeria’s second‑richest man, Abdul Samad Rabiu, expands into UAE food and logistics hub
item.description: Abdul Samad Rabiu, chairman of BUA Group and Nigeria’s second‑richest man, has signed a milestone Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates with AD Ports Group and MAIR Group to develop sugar refining, agro‑industrial projects, and integrated global logistics solutions.

item.title: UK scraps visa stickers for Nigerians in digital border overhaul
item.description: The United Kingdom will stop issuing physical visa stickers to Nigerian nationals from 25 February 2026, replacing them with mandatory electronic visas in what officials describe as a major step towards a fully digital border system.
